summary: Automate guest external-collab Slack channel provisioning with timeboxed access & Confluence read-only vault
description: Issue summary: Request to implement a standardized, auditable automation flow for provisioning Slack channels for external collaborators that are automatically linked to a read-only Confluence vault. Impact: Reduces manual admin work and improves auditability for external partner engagements; reduces risk of stale guest access. Current process: manual channel creation + ad-hoc Confluence share links; access expiry handled manually by requestor (often missed). Desired outcome: Self-service request in Jira or Slack that creates a channel with naming convention, invites guests for a timeboxed window, attaches a Confluence read-only space or page (using template), enforces automatic expiration and audit log export. Business justification: Frequent external collaborations (security partners, auditors, contractors) lead to inconsistent permissions and post-project access lingering. Automation will reduce support overhead, speed onboarding, and satisfy audit requirements. Request details: - Slack channel naming: ext-{org}-{project}-{yyMMDD} (bot enforces unique slug) - Channel created as private and guest-only (allow only invited members) - Guest invitations handled via SCIM/API where possible; alternatively via Slack workflow approving and escalating to Admin for non-SCIM orgs - Timebox: default 30 days with configurable options 7/30/90 days - Confluence: create a linked page/space using "External Collaboration Vault" template with read-only viewer group for external users; internal editors retained - Automated reminders: 7 days before expiry and on expiry notify channel and owner - Auto-revoke: remove external guests and archive channel; Confluence page set to internal-only archive mode - Audit exports: monthly CSV of channel membership changes and Confluence share history stored in compliance S3 bucket - Approval flow: requestor submits in Jira or Slack; workflow posts to #it-approvals channel; approver group (SecurityOps + WorkspaceAdmins) must approve within 48 hours; lack of response triggers escalation to SRE oncall - Edge cases: guests re-requesting access after expiry should create a new channel; emergency extensions require SecurityOps manual action.
acceptance_criteria: Provisioning flow can be initiated from a Jira request form and from a Slack slash command
Channel and Confluence vault are created automatically and linked within 1 hour of approval
Default timebox of 30 days enforced; guest accounts are revoked on expiry without manual steps
Automated 7-day pre-expiry reminders and expiry notifications are sent consistently
Monthly audit export contains channel membership delta and Confluence permission changes and is deposited to the compliance S3 path
Documentation and runbook created in Confluence with rollback steps and manual override process
Security review sign-off captured as part of workflow; no external guest can be elevated to admin in the channel
Unit/integration tests for automation scripts and QA runbook included in PR
proposed_implementation_steps: Design request form fields in Jira Service Desk: org name, project shortname, requested duration, point of contact, justification
Create Slack slash-command /ext-collab that opens request modal and posts to #it-approvals

Implement backend lambda that: validates request -> creates private Slack channel using naming convention -> invites guests via SCIM API or generates invite link when SCIM not possible -> creates Confluence page from template and links permissions
Hook into internal approval webhook that records approver response and timestamps in ticket
Implement scheduled job that runs daily to check expirations and trigger reminders/cleanup
Add audit export job that writes CSVs to s3://redwood-compliance/ext-collab-audits/
Build RBAC guardrails preventing elevation of external guest to channel admin; enforce via workspace app scopes and audit alerts
Create Confluence runbook describing manual offboarding, extension process, and emergency override steps
Open PR in infra/workspace-provisioner repo and include unit/integration tests; request SecurityOps review
rollout_plan: 1) Alpha: implement flow for 2 pilot teams (Security Partnerships, Legal) for 4 weeks. 2) Evaluate logs, gather feedback, adjust naming and duration options. 3) Beta: enable for platform and partnerships teams for 6 weeks with automated monitoring. 4) Full rollout: make self-service available to all internal teams, communicate policy, and retire manual request spreadsheet. Each stage includes audit sign-off and a 24-48h rollback window to disable automation if errors appear.
